# A floating component destroyed mid-mount still takes focus

## Context

Found while fixing #18838 (grid picker editors). A floating component that is shown and destroyed in the same App-Worker tick still focuses itself when its mount lands, and the focus is lost to `<body>` when the destroy's removal follows a few milliseconds later.

## The Problem

Reproducer on `examples/grid/cellEditing` with #18838's fix applied, at `dev@3f859a4803`: edit a date cell, open the picker by its trigger, pick a day, Escape (closes the picker), Enter. The DateField's own Enter handler shows its picker again (`form.field.Picker#onKeyDownEnter`), and in the same tick the grid's Enter ends the edit, destroying the editor and the picker. Main-thread trace (`focusin` / `focusout` capture listeners plus a body `MutationObserver`), 4 of 4 runs:

```
 3ms keydown Enter on #neo-datefield-1__input
 4ms added #neo-datefield-1__picker into BODY
 5ms focusout #neo-datefield-1__input -> #neo-grid-view-1      ← revertFocus, correct
 6ms focusin  #neo-grid-view-1
 6ms focusout #neo-grid-view-1 -> #neo-dateselector-1          ← the destroyed picker focuses itself
13ms removed #neo-datefield-1__picker from BODY (active now BODY)
```

With `me.focusOnMount && !me.isDestroyed && me.focus(me.id, true)` in `component.Base#afterSetMounted`, the same run keeps focus on `#neo-grid-view-1`; the picker still flashes into the DOM for ~9 ms and takes nothing.

The grid is only where it surfaced. Any floating component — menu, picker, tooltip, dialog — whose owner destroys it before its mount round trip returns has the same window.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/component/Base.mjs` `afterSetMounted` (`:762–783`): a floating component that mounts aligns and, with `focusOnMount`, focuses itself. `mounted` is written when the main thread confirms the insertion, which can be after `destroy()` ran in the App Worker; nothing there asks whether the instance still lives.
- `core.Base#destroy` sets `isDestroyed` (`src/core/Base.mjs:548`), the flag the rest of the engine reads for late async continuations.
- The mount delta and the removal delta travel separately, so the DOM node exists for a few milliseconds after the instance died — long enough for a focus call to land on it.

## The Fix

`component.Base#afterSetMounted` skips the alignment and the mount focus for a destroyed instance. One unit arm on a floating component: show, destroy in the same tick, then deliver the mount — no focus call goes out; the control (no destroy) still focuses.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A floating component destroyed before its mount confirmation lands sends no focus call and no `alignTo`.
- [ ] A floating component that stays alive still focuses on mount (`focusOnMount: true`) and still does not with `focusOnMount: false`.
- [ ] Unit arm red on `dev` first; the full unit and component tiers stay green.
- [ ] ~~On the public cellEditing example, Enter after a picker visit leaves focus on `grid.View` (e2e arm).~~ Moved: that arm needs this guard AND #18838's fix on `dev`, and what Enter means in a picker editor is interaction-contract scope of #18762 — it lands with that leaf. The main-thread trace in the PR is this ticket's receipt for the flow.

## Out of Scope

Whether a picker field should open its picker on Enter while it is a grid editor (the ~9 ms flash remains; interaction-contract scope of #18762) · `revertFocus()` losing its source after a visit to a second floating level — the pattern #18847 fixes in `menu.List` and #18838 fixes in the grid plugin, each locally.

## Avoided Traps

- **Hiding the picker from the grid plugin before it destroys the editor:** the mount delta is already in flight; the focus call comes from the mount confirmation, not from the show.
- **Unmounting synchronously in `destroy()`:** the removal delta cannot overtake a mount delta already sent.

## Related

#18838 · #18762 · #18847 (adjacent: focus falling to `<body>` when a floating level closes, different mechanism).
